targets.approach: Park for the Hermit Meadows trail, hike to the end-of-trail sign and keep going a few hundred metres, then drop down a steep slope into the canyon of the Hermit Narrows and head uphill. Baby Alpine is on the fourth wall up the canyon, the biggest crag.
targets.descent_text: After the finish, scramble up and over slabs to an alpine lake, then hike back down into the grassy gully at the foot of the wall.
targets.name: Baby Alpine

targets.approach: Park for the Hermit Meadows trail, hike to the end-of-trail sign and keep going a few hundred metres, then drop down a steep slope into the canyon of the Hermit Narrows and head uphill. Crystal Castle is on the right, on the third wall up, which has obvious white quartzite near the top.
targets.descent_text: Walk down the ledges on the skier's right into the gully below the Baby Alpine wall.
targets.name: Crystal Castle

targets.approach: Park for the Hermit Meadows trail, hike to the end-of-trail sign and keep going a few hundred metres, then drop down a steep slope into the canyon of the Hermit Narrows and head uphill. The route climbs the flakes on the right side of a huge chimney feature, and its belay tree is shared with Screams Across the Valley.
targets.name: Flake Alley

targets.approach: Park for the Hermit Meadows trail, hike to the end-of-trail sign and keep going a few hundred metres, then drop down a steep slope into the canyon of the Hermit Narrows and head uphill. The route is the right-most arete on the second wall, starting on large blocky ground just left of the arete.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route, or walk off either side.
targets.name: Screams Across the Valley

targets.approach: Park for the Hermit Meadows trail, hike to the end-of-trail sign and keep going a few hundred metres, then drop down a steep slope into the canyon of the Hermit Narrows and head uphill. The route is on the right side of the second wall, the obvious line right of Flake Alley, and it shares a belay tree with that route.
targets.name: Who even does this?

targets.approach: Reach the Joint Wall from the third highway pullout toward Gold River by hiking down the trail into the rocky river bed, or from the Crest Lake day-use area. The route shares its start with Above All Splendour, the right-most line on the wall, and then follows bolts to the left.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors.
targets.name: Above All Slander

targets.approach: Reach the Joint Wall from the Crest Lake day-use area by taking the trail past the picnic tables and bearing left at the fork, or from the third highway pullout toward Gold River by hiking down into the rocky river bed. The route is the right-most line on the wall, beginning on an arete a little beyond the tree line.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors at either belay.
targets.name: Above All Splendour

targets.approach: Drive the Kookipi Creek forest road to Branch 400 and follow it to the end of the usable road. From there bushwhack straight up into the alpine boulder field and keep climbing, skirting the foot of several big walls, to a huge face. The line begins at the face's left extreme, on splitter cracks.
targets.descent_text: Follow the dirt gully down and west to a notch heading a gully that returns to the foot of the climb.
targets.name: Back of Beyond Buttress

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Crest Lake day-use lot, cross the bridge and follow the signed trail; the Lower Hidden Walls are the first climbs reached. This is the first route you come to.
targets.name: Born to Wander

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Crest Lake day-use lot, cross the bridge and follow the signed trail; the Lower Hidden Walls are the first climbs reached. The route is just right of Snakebite and starts on large blocky ground below the anchors.
targets.name: Dragonfly Day

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Crest Lake day-use lot, cross the bridge and follow the signed trail; the Lower Hidden Walls are the first climbs reached. The route is beside The Accused but begins up on the ledge system, as the left-most route on that ledge.
targets.name: Obsured by Clouds

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Crest Lake day-use lot, cross the bridge and follow the signed trail; the Lower Hidden Walls are the first climbs reached. The route is the second obvious line on the wall, marked by a crack.
targets.name: The Accused

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Crest Lake day-use lot, cross the bridge and follow the signed trail; the Lower Hidden Walls are the first climbs reached. This is the right-most route on the Lower Hidden Walls.
targets.name: The Wolvercoon

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Crest Lake day-use lot, cross the bridge and follow the signed trail; the Lower Hidden Walls are the first climbs reached. The route begins up a crack and continues onto the steep bolted face above.
targets.name: Windweaver

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Crest Lake day-use lot, cross the bridge and follow the signed trail to the Lower Hidden Walls, then continue down toward the lake past Lady of the Lake. The route is next along the same trail.
targets.name: Dancing Days
targets.peak: Lower Hidden Walls (Lady of the Lake)

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Crest Lake day-use lot, cross the bridge and follow the signed trail to the Lower Hidden Walls, then keep going down the trail toward the lake. This is the first climb you reach, an obvious corner crack.
targets.name: Lady of the Lake
targets.peak: Lower Hidden Walls (Lady of the Lake)

targets.approach: Approach through New Crest and follow the signs to the Hidden Walls; the Middle Hidden Walls are the second tier of cliffs. The route is a finger-to-fist crack that starts partway up the wall, slightly overhanging, to the right of Shrunken Testicules.
targets.descent_text: Walk off from the bolted anchor, or rappel from the separate anchor to the left.
targets.name: Hidden Treasure

targets.approach: Approach through New Crest and follow the signs to the Hidden Walls; the Middle Hidden Walls are the second tier of cliffs. The route is toward the right side of the wall, starting on blocks.
targets.name: Spring Cleaning

targets.approach: Approach through New Crest and follow the signs to the Hidden Walls; the Middle Hidden Walls are the second tier of cliffs. The route begins directly next to the yew, midway along the wall.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors at the top.
targets.name: Stuck in the Middle with Yew

targets.approach: Approach through New Crest and follow the signs to the Hidden Walls; the Middle Hidden Walls are the second tier of cliffs. The route is on the right side of the wall, starting just left of the bulge at the same place as the 5.9 corner variation.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors at the top.
targets.name: Vicious Bastard

targets.approach: From the forest road off Highway 99 between Pemberton and Lillooet, park at the overgrown spur road. Hike up the old spur, crossing the first washed-out creek on a log, and where the road disappears into brush take the flagged, cairned climbers' trail uphill on the right. It runs alongside North Joffre Creek over boulders and alder, then drops to the creek's edge. Cross the creek when nearly below Mouse's Tooth and climb boulder fields to the foot of the left arete, with a large gully on its left.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route with two ropes. Bolted anchors are on every pitch but the fourth.
targets.name: Mighty Mouse

targets.approach: From the forest road off Highway 99 between Pemberton and Lillooet, park at the overgrown spur road and follow the flagged climbers' trail beside North Joffre Creek to the base of Mouse's Tooth, as for Mighty Mouse. The route begins by taking Mighty Mouse's opening two pitches up to the large ledge, then traverses right through a hanging garden to a hanging ledge below a steep, dirty corner.
targets.descent_text: Rappel Mighty Mouse.
targets.name: North Joffre Freak
North Nesakwatch Spire - NW Face Right(Neufeld/Struthers)

targets.descent_text: From the top, scramble south or southeast to a rappel station; one rope gets you down onto the south ridge. Scramble from there to the col between South Spire and Rexford, then descend the steep sandy gully, class 2 to 3 or snow-filled early in the season, to the basin.
targets.name: South Spire - North Ridge (AD-)

targets.approach: Aspirant Arete is on Petite Dione, close to the hut and just downhill from it, on the highway-shoulder side of Dione.
targets.name: Aspirant Arete

targets.approach: Phyllis' Engine is a group of granite spires along the crest linking Mt Carr and Castle Towers. From the Sphinx (Burton) Hut on the southeast side of Garibaldi Lake, climb glaciated terrain to the ridge. Climb the scree gully along the Engine's north side, then drop down on the east side and mantle a couple of large blocks to a small belay nook, which is the start.
targets.descent_text: Descend by the standard rappel route.
targets.name: Back Stack

targets.approach: Phyllis' Engine is a group of granite spires along the crest linking Mt Carr and Castle Towers. From the Sphinx (Burton) Hut on the southeast side of Garibaldi Lake, climb glaciated terrain to the ridge, then enter the scree gully on the north side of the Engine. The route starts at once, at a corner facing right, with a hand crack immediately beside it.
targets.name: Laminar Smoke

targets.approach: Phyllis' Engine is a group of granite spires along the crest linking Mt Carr and Castle Towers. From the Sphinx (Burton) Hut on the southeast side of Garibaldi Lake, climb glaciated terrain to the ridge. Three obvious cracks split the south wall below the highest smokestack; the route takes the right-most one, beside the corner.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from slung blocks.
targets.name: South Face Variation

targets.approach: Phyllis' Engine is a group of granite spires along the crest linking Mt Carr and Castle Towers. From the Sphinx (Burton) Hut on the southeast side of Garibaldi Lake, climb glaciated terrain to the ridge. Approach the face from the west and scramble to the foot of a corner on the right-hand side of the highest smokestack, which is the summit; that corner begins the first pitch.
targets.name: South West Face

targets.approach: The Pigeon Feathers are the shorter spires above the East Creek basin, reached from Applebee Dome or the Kain Hut. This route lies on Wide Awake Tower's south flank, the tower beyond the one holding Solitary Confinement. Walk up the snow gully on that side to the paired corners, one facing left and one facing right, on a pillar, and begin in the flare right under the corner that faces left, using a short pitch to reach the ledge when snow covers it.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route with two ropes. Not every rappel anchor sits at a belay, so note them on the way up; the anchors may need fresh cord.
targets.name: Electric Funeral

targets.approach: The Pigeon Feathers are the shorter spires above the East Creek basin, reached from Applebee Dome or the Kain Hut. The route is on the south face of West Peak, where obvious face-crack systems show from below. Start on a snow slope at a short dyke that leads to the left-arching finger crack.
targets.descent_text: Descend by rappel; some of the rappels are long enough that a tag line is needed.
targets.name: Fingerberry Jam

targets.approach: The Pigeon Feathers are the shorter spires above the East Creek basin, reached from Applebee Dome or the Kain Hut. The route is on the south face of Lost Feather Pinnacle: scramble up the talus and scree and keep traversing right to the first pitch.
targets.descent_text: Use two ropes to rappel from the bolted stations down the spire's west face.
targets.name: Furry Friends

targets.approach: The Pigeon Feathers are the shorter spires above the East Creek basin, reached from Applebee Dome or the Kain Hut. The route climbs Fingerberry Tower and can be seen from the snow arete linking the col between Pigeon and Howser and the East Creek basin. Drop into the scoop below that arete and scramble over boulders and crevasses to the crack system that leads to the big roof higher up.
targets.descent_text: Every belay is equipped with rappel hangers, so the route can be rappelled.
targets.name: Gravy Train

targets.approach: The Pigeon Feathers are the shorter spires above the East Creek basin, reached from Applebee Dome or the Kain Hut. The route is a splitter straight up the middle of Prince Albert Tower.
targets.descent_text: The anchors are bolted, so the route can be rappelled with two ropes.
targets.name: Solitary Confinement

targets.approach: The Pigeon Feathers are the shorter spires above the East Creek basin, reached from Applebee Dome or the Kain Hut. The route is on Wide Awake Tower, the tower past Prince Albert Tower, on the northwest face that looks toward Prince Albert Tower, a little uphill from the lowest part of the tower.
targets.name: Wild Fire

targets.approach: Queen Bess lies in the Coast Mountains with views of Mt Waddington and the Homathko Icefield. Access is by a charter flight, or by a very long walk in from Tatlayoko Lake. The route is the southeast buttress of the peak.
targets.name: SE Buttress

targets.approach: Follow the signs for Lower Sunrise to Roommate Rock. The route climbs flakes that trend leftward past bolts to the cracks and flakes on the arete.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors.
targets.name: The Odd Couple
